data.body: FORCE_CLOSE: close gate(s) bypassed by user approval — no completion/signature attestation was signed. Reason: "Substantive work COMPLETE and independently verified: 29,931 duplicate bot-authored Jira comments deleted across 27 of the 30 affected issues under the T4 safety plan the plan-review gate PASSED (full 150MB pre-deletion backup per issue with a fetched-equals-reported-total completeness gate before any DELETE; dry run produced and inspected; canary on one light issue verified three independent ways before the bulk run; keep-oldest-of-each-distinct-normalized-body using outbound_comments._normalize_comment_body reused verbatim; marker detection on pre-strip rendered ADF text; 0 non-candidate/human comments touched; 29,931-line deletion log). REB-1861 is out of the 5000 cap at 79; every affected issue now holds exactly one copy of each distinct body and is far below the cap. Verified independently of the tool's own check: a live-vs-backup diff over all 27 backed-up issues reports 0 missing distinct bodies and unchanged non-candidate counts everywhere. Forcing because the close gate's remaining objection is a tagging technicality, not a safety gap: it reads the artifact paths cited in the ACs (logs/dryrun-all.txt etc.) as repository-resident and therefore treats [non-codebase] as attestation laundering, but those artifacts live OUTSIDE this repo in ~/jira-cleanup-20260820/ (a one-time operational cleanup against live Jira; nothing in this repository changed, hence the recorded empty file impact). Resolving it means another description edit, which stales the freshly signed plan-review attestation and forces another review round — the same self-referential loop precedent bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f force-closed for. Phase 2 (836 truncation-suffix comments) was deliberately left unexecuted and reported for an operator decision; the marker-loss defect behind it is filed as 5931-78a3-95d2-44cd. The reconcile-bridge workflow remains PAUSED.". Session: eff19c3d-071a-47b5-bae6-8b48a3343a8c.
